relationships.subject: RvE1
relationships.evidence_quote: Strikingly, capsaicin-induced spontaneous pain is blocked by RvE1 (55).

relationships.subject: MaR1
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal administration of MaR1 (10 or 100 ng) alleviated nucleus pulposus-induced mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia for several days and reduced the activation of NLRP3-mediated inflammasome in rats (72).

relationships.subject: MaR1
relationships.evidence_quote: In a murine vulvar pain model, topical treatment of MaR1 not only reduced PGE2 levels but also alleviated mechanical pain (65).

relationships.subject: LXA4
relationships.evidence_quote: In primary culture of microglia, LXA4 inhibited TNF-α release through microglial ALX/FPR2 receptors (86).

relationships.subject: COX-2
relationships.evidence_quote: Importantly, COX-2 is required for thebiosynthesis of SPMs and resolution of inflammation (53, 54).

key_findings: Review: exogenous SPMs (RvD1, RvE1, MaR1, NPD1, LXA4) relieve inflammatory, postoperative, neuropathic and cancer pain in rodents, acting on glia, immune cells and neurons.
SPMs show distinct modulation of TRP channel-mediated pain, and neuromodulation such as vagus nerve stimulation increases endogenous SPMs.
